# Pathway Enrichment and Multi-Omics Abundance Profiles

Pathway enrichment and multi-omics profiling aggregate molecular alterations into functional signatures. This chapter covers Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), multi-omics pathway enrichment across RNA, single-cell transcriptomics, mass spectrometry proteomics, and microbiome metagenomics, bubble heatmap archetypes, and rank-abundance dynamic range curves.

## Gene Set Enrichment Analysis: `type = "gsea"` and `type = "gsea_running"`

Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (Subramanian et al., *PNAS* 2005) evaluates whether an a priori defined gene set $S$ shows cumulative enrichment at the extremes of a ranked gene list $L$:

$$P_{\text{hit}}(S, i) = \sum_{g_j \in S, j \le i} \frac{|r_j|^p}{N_R}, \quad N_R = \sum_{g_j \in S} |r_j|^p$$

$$P_{\text{miss}}(S, i) = \sum_{g_j \notin S, j \le i} \frac{1}{N - N_H}$$

$$ES(S) = \arg\max_{i} |P_{\text{hit}}(S, i) - P_{\text{miss}}(S, i)|$$

`cliomicplot` provides four complementary visualizations for GSEA results:
1. **Preranked Enrichment Dot Plot (`type = "gsea"`)**: Pathway terms ranked by effect magnitude, with dot size encoding $-\log_{10}(\text{FDR})$ and fill encoding Normalized Enrichment Score (NES).
2. **Three-Tier Running Score Walk Plot (`type = "gsea_running"`)**: The classical GSEA profile displaying the cumulative walk curve, gene hit barcode rug, and ranked metric area.
3. **Directional Diverging Lollipop Plot (`type = "lollipop"`)**: Horizontal effect size bars comparing positive and negative pathway activation.
4. **Multi-Phenotype Comparison Matrix (`type = type_bubble_diverging()`)**: Cross-condition pathway activity across disease phenotypes and therapeutic stages.

### Example 1: Preranked Pathway Enrichment Dot Plot

The dot plot displays top enriched pathways sorted by absolute NES, highlighting concurrent upregulation of inflammatory signaling and downregulation of lipid metabolism:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(cliomicplot)
library(ggplot2)

pathways <- c(
  "Cytokine-Cytokine Receptor Interaction", "JAK-STAT Signaling Pathway",
  "Toll-like Receptor Signaling", "Th1 and Th2 Cell Differentiation",
  "Chemokine Signaling Pathway", "NF-kappa B Signaling",
  "IL-17 Signaling Pathway", "Antigen Processing and Presentation",
  "T Cell Receptor Signaling", "B Cell Receptor Signaling",
  "Natural Killer Cell Mediated Cytotoxicity", "Apoptosis",
  "Fatty Acid Metabolism", "Steroid Biosynthesis", "Keratinization"
)

gsea_df <- data.frame(
  Term = pathways,
  NES  = c(2.65, 2.38, 2.15, 2.08, 1.95, 1.88, 1.72, 1.65, 1.45, 1.25, 0.95, 0.82, -1.65, -1.98, -2.45),
  FDR  = c(1e-5, 2e-5, 8e-5, 1e-4, 3e-4, 5e-4, 1e-3, 2e-3, 5e-3, 0.015, 0.045, 0.082, 0.002, 0.0005, 0.0001)
)

clitheme("nature")

p_gsea <- cliplot(
  gsea_df,
  type     = "gsea",
  top_term = 15,
  title    = "Normalized Enrichment Scores Across Inflammatory Cascades"
)
p_gsea
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](08-pathway-enrichment_files/figure-html/gsea-dotplot-demo-1.png){width=2400}
:::
:::


### Example 2: Three-Tier GSEA Running Enrichment Score Walk

The running enrichment score walk illustrates the cumulative enrichment score $ES(i)$ across ranked genes, identifying the leading-edge subset that accounts for peak enrichment:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(42)

# Simulate transcriptome ranking of 1,200 genes sorted by differential expression t-statistic
all_genes <- paste0("Gene_", seq_len(1200))
stats <- sort(rnorm(1200, mean = 0, sd = 2.0), decreasing = TRUE)
names(stats) <- all_genes

# Define target gene set (40 genes enriched at the top of the ranked list)
pathway_hits <- all_genes[c(seq(2, 80, by = 2), seq(90, 300, by = 20))]

# Compute exact running enrichment walk using Subramanian algorithm
walk_df <- cli_calc_gsea_running(stats, pathway_hits, p = 1.0)

# Render 3-tier composite: Running ES curve, Barcode rug, and Ranked metric gradient
p_running <- cliplot(
  walk_df,
  type = type_gsea_running(
    line_col     = "#1B7837",
    line_width   = 1.1,
    barcode_col  = "#182033",
    show_metric  = TRUE,
    peak_color   = "#D73027",
    pathway_name = "Hallmark IL-4 / IL-13 Signaling Pathway",
    nes          = 2.45,
    fdr          = 0.0001
  )
)
p_running
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](08-pathway-enrichment_files/figure-html/gsea-running-demo-1.png){width=2460}
:::
:::


### Example 3: Directional Diverging Lollipop Enrichment Plot

Horizontal lollipops provide a clean visualization of pathway activation versus repression relative to the zero null baseline:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pathway_subset <- c(
  "Cytokine-Cytokine Receptor", "JAK-STAT Cascade", "Th2 Differentiation",
  "Chemokine Cascade", "NF-kB Activation", "IL-17 Signaling",
  "Fatty Acid Metabolism", "Keratinization", "Steroid Biosynthesis"
)
nes_subset <- c(2.65, 2.38, 2.08, 1.95, 1.88, 1.72, -1.65, -1.98, -2.45)

lollipop_df <- data.frame(
  Term = pathway_subset,
  NES  = nes_subset,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
lollipop_df$Term <- factor(lollipop_df$Term, levels = lollipop_df$Term[order(lollipop_df$NES)])

clitheme("science")

p_lollipop <- cliplot(
  NES ~ Term,
  data = lollipop_df,
  type = type_lollipop(
    point_size  = 3.8,
    stem_width  = 0.8,
    point_color = "#3B4992"
  ),
  title = "Directional Pathway Enrichment Relative to Zero Baseline",
  xlab  = "Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)"
) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4)
p_lollipop
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](08-pathway-enrichment_files/figure-html/gsea-lollipop-demo-1.png){width=2400}
:::
:::


### Example 4: Multi-Phenotype GSEA Comparison Matrix

Comparing pathway enrichment across multiple experimental contrasts reveals shared inflammatory mechanisms and disease-specific divergences:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(101)
pheno_pathways <- c(
  "IL-4 / IL-13 Signaling", "Th2 Differentiation", "JAK-STAT Cascade",
  "Chemokine Receptor Activity", "Epidermal Differentiation", "Lipid Synthesis"
)
comparisons <- c("AD LS vs Healthy", "AD NL vs Healthy", "AD LS vs NL", "Dupilumab W16")

multi_gsea <- expand.grid(Pathway = pheno_pathways, Comparison = comparisons, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
multi_gsea$NES <- c(
  2.6, 0.8, 2.1, -1.8,
  2.3, 0.5, 1.9, -1.6,
  1.9, 0.6, 1.5, -1.2,
  2.0, 0.4, 1.7, -1.1,
  -2.4, -0.6, -2.1, 1.8,
  -2.1, -0.4, -1.8, 1.5
)
multi_gsea$FDR <- c(
  1e-4, 0.08, 2e-4, 5e-4,
  3e-4, 0.12, 4e-4, 8e-4,
  2e-3, 0.10, 5e-3, 0.01,
  1e-3, 0.15, 3e-3, 0.02,
  2e-4, 0.09, 3e-4, 1e-3,
  5e-4, 0.14, 8e-4, 2e-3
)

clitheme("nature")

p_multi_gsea <- cliplot(
  Pathway ~ Comparison,
  data       = multi_gsea,
  by         = -log10(multi_gsea$FDR),
  type       = type_bubble_diverging(
    palette      = "nature",
    midpoint     = 0,
    max_size     = 7.5,
    stroke_col   = "grey30",
    stroke_width = 0.35,
    size_name    = expression(-log[10]~italic(q)),
    fill_name    = "NES"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = multi_gsea$NES),
  title      = "Cross-Phenotype Pathway Enrichment Concordance",
  subtitle   = "Circle size encodes -log10 q; fill encodes Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)"
)
p_multi_gsea
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](08-pathway-enrichment_files/figure-html/gsea-comparison-matrix-demo-1.png){width=2550}
:::

## Multi-Omics Pathway Enrichment: RNA, Single-Cell, Proteomics, and Microbiome

Enrichment analysis bridges high-dimensional omics measurements to functional biological mechanisms. Different molecular layers require specialized metric encodings:
- **Bulk RNA-seq**: Gene ratio (fraction of pathway members meeting differential expression cutoffs) and FDR significance tiers.
- **Single-cell RNA-seq**: Cell-type-resolved signature activation scores paired with the percentage of expressing cells.
- **Mass Spectrometry Proteomics**: Fold enrichment of detected peptide sets combined with directional protein $\log_2(\text{FC})$.
- **Microbial Metagenomics**: Differential MetaCyc pathway abundance across anatomical microenvironments and dysbiotic states.

### Bulk RNA-seq Over-Representation Analysis (ORA)

In bulk transcriptomics, Over-Representation Analysis determines whether genes of a pathway $S$ appear in the significant differentially expressed gene (DEG) set $D$ more frequently than expected by chance under a hypergeometric distribution:

$$P(X \ge k) = \sum_{i=k}^{\min(|S|, |D|)} \frac{\binom{|S|}{i} \binom{N - |S|}{|D| - i}}{\binom{N}{|D|}}$$

The Gene Ratio $\frac{k}{|D|}$ reflects pathway coverage, with point size denoting significant gene count and fill denoting $-\log_{10}(\text{FDR})$:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
rna_ora_df <- data.frame(
  Term = c(
    "IL-4 and IL-13 Signaling", "Th2 Immune Activation", "Keratinocyte Hyperproliferation",
    "S100 Alarmin Cascade", "Antimicrobial Peptide Defense", "Epidermal Barrier Assembly",
    "Fatty Acid Elongation", "Sphingolipid Biosynthesis"
  ),
  GeneRatio = c(0.44, 0.39, 0.34, 0.30, 0.27, 0.23, 0.17, 0.14),
  Count     = c(31, 24, 18, 15, 13, 17, 11, 9),
  FDR       = c(1.5e-8, 4.2e-7, 1.1e-5, 2.8e-5, 7.5e-5, 1.8e-4, 9.5e-4, 3.8e-3),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
rna_ora_df$Term <- factor(rna_ora_df$Term, levels = rna_ora_df$Term[order(rna_ora_df$GeneRatio)])

clitheme("nature")

p_rna_ora <- ggplot2::ggplot(rna_ora_df, ggplot2::aes(x = GeneRatio, y = Term)) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    ggplot2::aes(x = 0, xend = GeneRatio, y = Term, yend = Term),
    color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    ggplot2::aes(size = Count, fill = -log10(FDR)),
    shape = 21, color = "grey25", stroke = 0.45
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = c("#EFF3FF", "#6BAED6", "#2171B5", "#08519C"),
    name = expression(-log[10]~italic(q))
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_size_area(max_size = 7.5, name = "DEG Count") +
  theme_cli_nature() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Gene Ratio (k / |D|)",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Bulk Transcriptomic Over-Representation Analysis (Lesional vs Healthy)",
    subtitle = "Gene ratio denotes pathway representation; point size reflects significant DEG count"
  )
p_rna_ora
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](08-pathway-enrichment_files/figure-html/multiomics-rna-ora-1.png){width=2550}
:::
:::


### Single-Cell scRNA-seq Cell-Type-Resolved Pathway Signatures

Single-cell pathway scoring (e.g. AUCell or UCell module scores) decomposes pathway activity across specific cellular lineages:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
sc_pathways <- c(
  "Type 2 Cytokine Cascade", "IL-17 Response", "Alarmin Signaling",
  "Epidermal Differentiation", "Antigen Presentation", "Extracellular Matrix Remodeling"
)
cell_types <- c(
  "Basal KC", "Spinous KC", "Suprabasal KC", "CD4+ Th2", "ILC2", "cDC2", "Fibroblasts"
)

sc_df <- expand.grid(Pathway = sc_pathways, CellType = cell_types, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
sc_df$PctActive <- c(
  15, 8, 35, 92, 84, 18, 12,
  12, 10, 22, 18, 25, 14, 8,
  78, 65, 82, 12, 15, 45, 22,
  95, 98, 92, 4, 2, 8, 6,
  18, 14, 20, 32, 28, 96, 24,
  8, 6, 10, 5, 4, 15, 94
)
sc_df$Score <- c(
  0.15, 0.05, 0.42, 1.85, 1.62, 0.22, 0.10,
  0.08, 0.04, 0.18, 0.22, 0.31, 0.12, 0.05,
  1.42, 1.15, 1.58, 0.10, 0.15, 0.65, 0.25,
  1.92, 2.10, 1.88, -0.05, -0.08, 0.05, 0.02,
  0.22, 0.15, 0.25, 0.45, 0.38, 1.95, 0.30,
  0.05, 0.02, 0.08, 0.01, 0.00, 0.12, 1.88
)

clitheme("cell")

p_sc_path <- cliplot(
  Pathway ~ CellType,
  data = sc_df,
  by   = sc_df$PctActive,
  type = type_bubble_circle(
    palette      = "plasma",
    max_size     = 7.5,
    stroke_col   = "grey35",
    stroke_width = 0.35,
    size_name    = "% Active Cells",
    fill_name    = "Mean Score"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = sc_df$Score),
  title      = "Cell-Type-Resolved Pathway Activation in Inflammatory Skin",
  subtitle   = "Point size reflects percentage of active cells; colour reflects mean module score"
)
p_sc_path
```

### Mass Spectrometry Proteomics Functional Module Enrichment

Skin tissue mass spectrometry proteomics measures translated protein abundance. Functional modules (cornified envelope, desmosomes, serine peptidase inhibitors, and antimicrobial peptides) are tracked across clinical lesions:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
modules <- c(
  "Cornified Envelope (FLG, LOR, IVL)", "Desmosome Assembly (DSC1, DSG1)",
  "Serine Peptidase Inhibitors (SPINK5)", "Antimicrobial Defense (S100A7, DEFB4A)",
  "Extracellular Matrix Assembly", "Mitochondrial OxPhos"
)
conditions <- c("AD Lesional", "AD Non-Lesional", "Psoriasis Lesional", "Healthy Control")

prot_df <- expand.grid(Module = modules, Condition = conditions, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
prot_df$Log2FC <- c(
  -2.45, -0.85, -1.95, 0.00,
  -1.85, -0.62, -1.45, 0.00,
  2.65, 0.95, 1.82, 0.00,
  3.10, 1.15, 3.85, 0.00,
  1.35, 0.45, 0.95, 0.00,
  -1.45, -0.32, -1.15, 0.00
)
prot_df$negLogQ <- c(
  7.8, 3.2, 6.1, 0.2,
  5.4, 2.1, 4.8, 0.1,
  6.9, 3.5, 5.2, 0.3,
  8.5, 4.1, 9.2, 0.2,
  4.1, 1.8, 3.2, 0.1,
  4.8, 1.5, 3.9, 0.2
)

clitheme("nature")

p_prot_mod <- cliplot(
  Module ~ Condition,
  data       = prot_df,
  by         = prot_df$negLogQ,
  type       = type_bubble_diverging(
    palette      = "nature",
    midpoint     = 0,
    max_size     = 8.0,
    stroke_col   = "grey30",
    stroke_width = 0.4,
    size_name    = expression(-log[10]~italic(q)),
    fill_name    = expression(log[2]~"FC (Protein)")
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = prot_df$Log2FC),
  title      = "Mass Spectrometry Deep Proteomics Functional Module Enrichment",
  subtitle   = "Circle size encodes -log10 q; diverging fill encodes protein abundance log2(FC)"
)
p_prot_mod
```

### Skin & Gut Microbiome Functional Metagenomics (MetaCyc Pathways)

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}

)

mb_df <- expand.grid(Pathway = metacyc_paths, Site = sites, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
mb_df$Log2FC <- c(
  3.15, 2.45, 1.85, 1.95,
  2.40, 1.82, 1.45, 1.55,
  1.95, 1.40, 0.95, 1.15,
  -2.25, -1.65, -1.15, -1.35,
  -1.75, -1.25, -0.85, -0.95,
  -1.45, -0.95, -0.65, -0.75
)
mb_df$negLogQ <- c(
  6.8, 5.2, 3.9, 4.2,
  5.5, 4.1, 3.2, 3.5,
  4.2, 3.1, 2.1, 2.5,
  5.1, 3.8, 2.8, 3.1,
  3.9, 2.8, 1.8, 2.2,
  3.2, 2.1, 1.5, 1.8
)

clitheme("nature")

p_mb_metacyc <- cliplot(
```

## Bubble Heatmap Archetypes: `type = "bubble_heatmap"`

Bubble heatmaps display two continuous variables across features (rows) and conditions (columns). Point size encodes magnitude, count, or significance; fill colour encodes directional effect size ($\log_2\text{FC}$, NES) or continuous significance ($-\log_{10}P$).

`cliomicplot` provides five bubble forms:
1. **Diamond Bubble Matrix**: classic diamond glyphs with alternating row bands.
2. **Circular Dot Bubble Matrix with Divergent Palette**: circular dots centered on zero to show positive and negative regulation.
3. **Significance-Glyph Annotated Matrix**: bubbles with significance asterisks (`*`, `**`, `***`) based on adjusted $P$-values.
4. **Square / Tile-Scaled Matrix**: proportional square glyphs in a tile grid.
5. **Directional Triangle Bubble Matrix**: oriented triangles indicating directional modulation across experimental cohorts.

### Form 1: Classic Diamond Bubble Matrix

Diamond bubble matrices display effect magnitude as diamond area and statistical significance as fill colour. Values exceeding `label_threshold` are labelled directly inside the glyphs.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(42)
proteins <- c("APOE", "MAPT", "APP", "SNCA", "GFAP", "NEFL", "VIM", "SYN1", "GAP43", "UCHL1")
contrasts <- c("AD vs Control", "PD vs Control", "AD vs PD", "Severe vs Mild")

bh_df <- expand.grid(Protein = proteins, Comparison = contrasts, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
bh_df$absFC <- runif(nrow(bh_df), 0.2, 3.5)
bh_df$negLogP <- runif(nrow(bh_df), 1.0, 15.0)

clitheme("cell")

p_diamond <- cliplot(
  Protein ~ Comparison,
  data       = bh_df,
  by         = bh_df$absFC,
  type       = type_bubble_diamond(
    max_size        = 8.0,
    size_name       = "|log2FC|",
    fill_name       = expression(-log[10]~P),
    fill_low        = "#4575B4",
    fill_mid        = "#FFFFBF",
    fill_high       = "#D73027"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = bh_df$negLogP),
  title      = "Diamond Bubble Matrix: Neurodegenerative Biomarkers",
  subtitle   = "Point size reflects |log2FC|; colour gradient reflects -log10 P"
)
p_diamond
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](08-pathway-enrichment_files/figure-html/bubble-diamond-demo-1.png){width=2550}
:::
:::


### Form 2: Circular Dot Bubble Matrix with Divergent Palette

For bidirectional metrics such as Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) or signed $\log_2\text{FC}$, `type_bubble_diverging()` applies a diverging colour gradient centered at 0 (e.g. `palette = "nature"`: navy to white to red). Bubble radius represents $-\log_{10}q$.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(101)
pathways_circ <- c(
  "IL-4 / IL-13 Signaling", "Th2 Differentiation", "JAK-STAT Cascade",
  "NF-kB Activation", "Epidermal Barrier", "Keratinization",
  "Lipid Metabolism", "Interferon Gamma Response"
)
stages <- c("Acute Lesional", "Chronic Lesional", "Non-Lesional", "Dupilumab W16")

da_df <- expand.grid(Pathway = pathways_circ, Stage = stages, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
da_df$NES <- c(
  2.4, 2.8, 0.4, -1.8,
  2.1, 2.5, 0.2, -1.5,
  1.8, 2.2, 0.5, -1.2,
  1.9, 1.7, 0.3, -0.9,
  -2.2, -2.6, -0.3, 1.9,
  -2.5, -3.1, -0.5, 2.2,
  -1.7, -2.1, -0.2, 1.4,
  0.6, 1.2, 0.1, -0.4
)
da_df$negLogQ <- runif(nrow(da_df), 1.5, 12.0)

clitheme("nature")

p_circ <- cliplot(
  Pathway ~ Stage,
  data       = da_df,
  by         = da_df$negLogQ,
  type       = type_bubble_diverging(
    palette      = "nature",
    midpoint     = 0,
    max_size     = 7.5,
    stroke_col   = "grey30",
    stroke_width = 0.35,
    size_name    = expression(-log[10]~italic(q)),
    fill_name    = "NES"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = da_df$NES),
  title      = "Inflammatory Pathway Modulation Across Disease Stages",
  subtitle   = "Circle size encodes -log10 q; diverging fill encodes Normalized Enrichment Score"
)
p_circ
```

### Form 3: Significance-Glyph Overlaid Matrix

When statistical significance requires explicit discrete thresholds ($* p < 0.05$, $** p < 0.01$, $*** p < 0.001$), `label_metric = "signif"` prints asterisks directly onto the bubbles.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(202)
cytokines <- c("IL4", "IL13", "IL22", "IL31", "CCL17", "CCL18", "CCL26", "CXCL10", "IFNG", "IL1B")
timepoints <- c("Baseline", "Week 4", "Week 16", "Week 52")

cyt_df <- expand.grid(Cytokine = cytokines, Timepoint = timepoints, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cyt_df$log2FC <- runif(nrow(cyt_df), 0.2, 4.0)
cyt_df$negLogP <- runif(nrow(cyt_df), 0.5, 8.0)

clitheme("science")

p_signif <- cliplot(
  Cytokine ~ Timepoint,
  data       = cyt_df,
  by         = cyt_df$log2FC,
  type       = type_bubble_heatmap(
    shape          = "circle",
    palette        = "viridis",
    label_metric   = "signif",
    signif_cutoffs = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
    label_size     = 3.2,
    label_col      = "white",
    stroke_col     = "grey35",
    stroke_width   = 0.4,
    size_name      = expression(log[2]~"FC"),
    fill_name      = expression(-log[10]~P)
  ),
```

### Form 4: Square / Tile-Scaled Matrix

Proportional squares in a tile grid display cell density, taxon abundance, or cross-cohort concordance.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(303)
taxa <- c("S. aureus", "S. epidermidis", "C. acnes", "M. restricta", "P. melaninogenica", "C. striatum")
sites <- c("Volar Forearm", "Antecubital Fossa", "Forehead", "Cheek", "Retroauricular")

taxa_df <- expand.grid(Taxon = taxa, Site = sites, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
taxa_df$Abundance <- runif(nrow(taxa_df), 1.0, 30.0)
taxa_df$Prevalence <- runif(nrow(taxa_df), 20.0, 95.0)

clitheme("nejm")

p_square <- cliplot(
  Taxon ~ Site,
  data       = taxa_df,
  by         = taxa_df$Abundance,
  type       = type_bubble_square(
    palette      = "mako",
    max_size     = 8.0,
    stroke_col   = "white",
    stroke_width = 0.5,
    size_name    = "Rel. Abund (%)",
    fill_name    = "Prevalence (%)"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = taxa_df$Prevalence),
  title      = "Microbial Colonization Density Across Skin Microenvironments",
  subtitle   = "Square area reflects relative abundance; fill intensity reflects cohort prevalence"
)
p_square
```

### Form 5: Directional Triangle Bubble Matrix

Directional triangles (`shape = "triangle_up"` or `"triangle_down"`) emphasize activation or repression across experimental screens.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(404)
genes <- c("STAT3", "STAT6", "GATA3", "TBX21", "RORC", "FOXP3", "NFKB1", "RELA")
treatments <- c("Vehicle", "IL-4 Stim", "JAKi (Baricitinib)", "Biologic (Dupilumab)")

tri_df <- expand.grid(Gene = genes, Treatment = treatments, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
tri_df$Score <- runif(nrow(tri_df), 0.5, 5.0)
tri_df$Activity <- runif(nrow(tri_df), 1.0, 10.0)

clitheme("nature")

p_tri <- cliplot(
  Gene ~ Treatment,
  data       = tri_df,
  by         = tri_df$Score,
  type       = type_bubble_heatmap(
    shape        = "triangle_up",
    palette      = "rocket",
    grid_style   = "banded",
    max_size     = 8.0,
    stroke_col   = "white",
    stroke_width = 0.6,
    size_name    = "TF Score",
    fill_name    = "Activity Index"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = tri_df$Activity),
  title      = "Transcription Factor Activity Profile",
  subtitle   = "Triangle area encodes binding score; fill denotes computed activity index"
)
p_tri
```

## Rank-Abundance Dynamic Range Curves: `type = "rankabundance"`

In quantitative proteomics, rank-abundance curves visualize the dynamic range of protein detection across orders of magnitude:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(42)
n_prot <- 800
intensities <- sort(10^rnorm(n_prot, mean = 6.5, sd = 1.1), decreasing = TRUE)
ranks <- seq_len(n_prot)

rank_df <- data.frame(
  Rank      = ranks,
  Intensity = intensities,
  Protein   = paste0("Prot_", ranks)
)

clitheme("science")

p_rank <- cliplot(
  Intensity ~ Rank,
  data = rank_df,
  type = type_rankabundance(
    log_scale     = "10",
    point_color   = "#4DBBD5",
    marginal_type = "density",
    label_genes   = c("Prot_1", "Prot_10", "Prot_50", "Prot_200"),
    label_color   = "#E64B35",
    label_size    = 3.0
  ),
  title    = "Dynamic Range of Proteome Detection",
  subtitle = "Protein abundance spanning ~5 orders of magnitude with marginal density",
  xlab     = "Abundance Rank",
  ylab     = "LFQ Intensity"
)
p_rank
```
